title: Interstate Road Transport Charge Amendment Bill (No. 2) 2008
portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government

speeches.speaker: Nick Sherry
speeches.brief: The speaker moved that the bills be taken together and read a first time without formalities, and the motion was agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Nick Sherry
speeches.brief: The speech announced the introduction of several bills, including education legislation that appropriates over $0.5 billion for Indigenous education programs from 2009 to 2012, and a Schools Assistance Bill providing $28 billion for non-government schools, with a focus on closing Indigenous educational gaps. It also introduced revised heavy vehicle registration charges to end cross-subsidisation, a road user charge increase to 21 cents per litre, and a $70 million Heavy Vehicle Safety and Productivity Package.

speeches.speaker: Ian Macdonald
speeches.brief: The coalition supported the first bill on interstate heavy vehicle registration charges but opposed the second bill's increase in the road user charge to 21 cents per litre without safeguards. The coalition announced amendments to prevent any future indexation of the charge, require at least 50 additional heavy-vehicle rest areas per year, and link increases to harmonisation of state transport regulations.

speeches.speaker: Carol Brown
speeches.brief: The speaker proposed that officials from the government, opposition, and Senator Fielding meet during lunch to coordinate overlapping amendment requests for the Road Charges Legislation Repeal and Amendment Bill 2008, in order to minimise debate time. The opposition insisted that the road user charge not increase unless the government demonstrates it spends more on roads than it collects from the industry, and also demanded provisions for additional heavy-vehicle rest areas and harmonisation.

speeches.speaker: Ian Macdonald
speeches.brief: The Senate considered the Road Charges Legislation Repeal and Amendment Bill 2008, raising the road user charge from 19 cents to 21 cents per litre, with government amendments removing automatic indexation and making future increases disallowable ministerial determinations. The chamber agreed to opposition requests banning indexation methods and limiting increases to one per financial year, while rejecting requests to tie future increases to the construction of 50 rest areas per year and to delay collection until after disallowance; Family First's request for a review of the Heavy Vehicle Safety and Productivity Program, linked to a $70 million truck stop package, was also agreed.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Conroy
speeches.brief: The committee report was adopted. The speaker supported the original bill but opposed the Road Charges Legislation Repeal and Amendment Bill 2008.
